summary: Verified the cookie-scheme fix. Added tests/test_cookie_params.py (unit-tests auth.cookie_params() with importlib.reload for http, http+IP, https, and empty FRONTEND_URL) and tests/test_https_cookie_regression.py (hosted preview: login sets access_token with Secure; SameSite=None; HttpOnly and /api/auth/me works). Ran full pytest suite: 13/13 passed in 64s. Existing backend regression (auth, businesses, node-pairs, demo seed, dashboard, runs, incidents, async compare, invalid incident status) all green — fix did not regress hosted HTTPS behavior.
critical_code_review_comments: auth.cookie_params() only checks prefix 'https://' — a FRONTEND_URL like 'HTTPS://...' (uppercase) or with a leading space would fall through to non-secure. Minor, low risk given env is controlled.

logout endpoint deletes cookies without passing the same secure/samesite flags used to set them; some browsers require matching attributes to clear cookies. Not a bug for functionality but worth aligning.
seed_data_creation: Used existing /api/demo/seed endpoint invoked by existing tests; created + deleted TEST_biz/TEST_np during business CRUD test.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Cookie-scheme fix is fully covered: unit tests reload auth module across http/https FRONTEND_URL values and assert exact flags dict; HTTPS regression asserts real Set-Cookie header contains Secure, SameSite=None, HttpOnly. teardown restores env for other tests. All 13 backend tests pass.
rca of the issue: Original bug: set_cookie hardcoded secure=True, samesite='none'. Browsers drop such cookies over plain HTTP on non-localhost origins, so docker-compose HTTP self-hosted deployments logged in with 200 but never persisted the session. Fix introduces cookie_params() that inspects FRONTEND_URL scheme: https -> Secure+None, otherwise -> non-Secure+Lax. Unit tests confirm both branches; hosted HTTPS regression confirms preview still gets Secure;SameSite=None and /me returns admin.
